sources.note: Nothing on stress, accent or tone (0 hits for stress/tone/tonal/accent/pitch/prosod/syllable in the 52-page chapter). The Mangree section is classificatory: 'Oldendorp (2000: 382) noted that a great river, which must be either the Sassandra or the Bandama (cf. Fodor 1975: 162), constituted the border between the "Gien" and the "Mangree," and that their languages "[did] not differ much from one another" (Highfield & Barac 1987: 162). Oldendorp recorded no "Mangree" numerals.. Thus, the "Mangree" could correspond to the Ngere (or Wee) of the Ivory Coast (cf. Jones 2010: 186; Oldendorp 2000: 381…

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonology content. Ethnographic account only (scarification, neighbours Kanga/Mandinga/Amina, warfare, religion: 'Gott hiess in ihrem Lande Jankombum.. Teufel, nennen ihn Didi', burial, priests, poison ordeal). Adds two lexical items in context (Jankombum 'God', Didi 'devil', both said to be shared with Amina) but no remark on pronunciation, accent or tone. Confirms that even the unabridged Oldendorp edition's Mangree account carries no phonological description.

sources.citation: Fodor, István. 1975. Pallas und andere afrikanische Vokabularien vor dem 19. Jahrhundert: Ein Beitrag zur Forschungsgeschichte. Hamburg: Buske. Section 7.91 'Mangree', pp. 162-164 (full transcription hosted at Wikipedia:WikiProject Languages/Mangree source).
sources.note: Nothing. Fodor reprints Oldendorp's 11 words, notes 'OLD gibt keinen Beispielsatz aus dem Mangree an', discusses possible Twi/Ewe/Kru/pidgin look-alikes, and concludes 'So bleibt das Mangree unidentifiziert.' No phonological commentary beyond the name's pronunciation (mangre: / mangrɛi). (Transcription saved as the.wiki file; the printed book itself was not opened.)

sources.citation: Christaller, J. G. 1889. Die Sprachen in dem Negerfreistaat Liberia. Zeitschrift für afrikanische Sprachen 2 (Oktober 1888 - Juli 1889): 315-320. Berlin: Asher. [Mangree remark on p. 320]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonology of Mangree. The only Mangree content is a classificatory remark (p. 320): 'OLDENDORPs Sprachproben stimmen mit Kru in Kanga und meist auch in Gien, in Mangree nur teilweise; die betr. Negerin mischte auch zwei Asante-Wörter (für Gott und Kopf) und ein portugiesisches (pikkenine für Kind) mit ein.' i.e. the Mangree words agree with Kru only partly and include two Asante loans and one Portuguese word. (The article does remark on Kru vowel qualities, not on Mangree.)

sources.note: Nothing. The primary source: an ethnographic note on the 'Mangree' nation (pp. 276-277: neighbours of the Kanga, a large river separates them from the Gian, languages 'wenig verschieden') and 11 concept words in the comparative vocabulary table (Gott Jankombum, Himmel Tata, Sonne Lataa..). No sentences, no numerals, no remarks on pronunciation or accent.
